summary: Populates a PNG-style image-descriptor struct (a2) from scalar arguments: width, height, bit depth, color-type and flag bytes, then computes a row factor and rowbytes. If the width would overflow row-size arithmetic it dispatches the error string aWidthTooLargeT ("Width too large to process image data; rowbytes will overflow.") via CallbackDispatch and stores rowbytes as 0. No-op unless both a1 and a2 are non-null.

operations.description: Only proceed when a1 and a2 are both non-null; otherwise do nothing.
byte at a2+29 = 1 when a6 equals 3 or (a6 & 2) is zero, otherwise 3.
If (a6 & 4) is non-zero, increment byte at a2+29.
byte at a2+30 = v9 = a5 * byte at a2+29 (bit depth scaled by row factor).

When a3 <= 0x7FFFFFFF / ((v9 + 7) >> 3), store rowbytes = (a3 * v9 + 7) >> 3 at a2+12; otherwise dispatch the aWidthTooLargeT string ("Width too large to process image data; rowbytes will overflow.") via CallbackDispatch(a1, ...) and store rowbytes = 0.

clean_pseudocode: setup_image_info(a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8, a9)
byte(a2+26) = a8;  byte(a2+27) = a9;  byte(a2+28) = a7;
unresolved: Exact semantics of the flag bytes a6/a7/a8/a9 and of descriptor fields at a2+29 and a2+30.
The relation of the row-factor derivation to a concrete PNG color type.
Role of the error-string global aWidthTooLargeT beyond being the dispatched message.
